schemes.description: Final-year Arts subject in which students work in a small consulting team on a real project identified by an external industry partner. Projects run mainly on campus under a faculty academic supervisor; hosts meet students at the start of semester, receive a check-in around week six and attend in-person final presentations. Past outputs include marketing strategies, advertising materials, website design, program appraisals and event proposals.
schemes.admin_host: Faculty of Arts (Experiential Learning team)
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Bachelor of Arts students; also available as a breadth option for approved courses (courses not listed in the extract).
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: 2018 handbook prerequisite: completion of 150 points of the Bachelor of Arts (not verified for 2026). Self-enrolment via study plan.
schemes.credit_assessment: 12.5 points. 2020 handbook assessment: 10-minute presentation (20%), 1,500-word project summary (40%), 1,500-word project proposal (40%); 80% seminar attendance hurdle. 2026 assessment not retrieved.
schemes.delivery_format: On campus (Parkville), seminars plus team project
schemes.project_evidence: Students 'collaborate on a real project for an actual industry partner'; outputs include marketing strategies, website design, program appraisals and event proposals [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: 'as part of a small consulting team' [1]; host collaborates 'with a small team of our students' [2].
schemes.employer_evidence: Partner identifies the project, meets students at start of semester, receives a check-in about six weeks later and attends in-person presentations at semester's end [2].
schemes.partner_role: Sets project/brief; meets team; receives final presentation. Academic supervises.
schemes.deliverable: Project outputs for partner (e.g. strategy, materials, appraisal) plus presentation; assessed proposal and summary.
schemes.unresolved: Partner sector mix not evidenced (pages say 'international and domestic partners'). 2026 assessment and prerequisite tabs not indexed. Subject code appears as ART300001 on one faculty page (typo).

profile_md:
**University of Melbourne** has distributed, mostly faculty-level provision of team projects for external organisations rather than one institution-wide scheme.

- **Compulsory capstones with external clients** are strongest at graduate level: the Master of IT *Software Project* (COMP90082) and Master of Software Engineering *Advanced Software Project* (SWEN90017/18, 'large teams... for an external client'), and the Faculty of Science capstone Industry Project model (teams of 3-5 on partner-submitted briefs) in the Masters of Data Science (MAST90106/7, 2026), Biotechnology (SCIE90015) and Environmental Science. The Master of Engineering capstone (ENGR90037/38) is group-based but involves industry partners only 'where appropriate'; Electrical & Electronic Engineering documents an industry-supervised team route.
- **Elective/selective curricular routes**: Arts *Industry Project* (ARTS30001, small consulting teams for partners who brief and attend presentations, also open as breadth); FBE *Management Consulting* (MGMT30012, teams assigned to client organisations, quota); *Creating Innovative Professionals* (ENGR90039, multidisciplinary teams on sponsor challenges, open to specified programs across Engineering/IT, FBE and Design); Law's Indigenous Legal Advocacy Clinic (partner-briefed, group format unclear in 2025).
- **Extracurricular**: FBE-only Business Innovation Challenge (2 days) and Virtual Industry Projects (25 hours, Practera-matched live clients); cross-faculty SCOUT (CAS Energy, 2026) and IPP O-Lab (status undated).

Partners mostly act as brief-setters/clients; sector mix is rarely documented. No route is university-wide in eligibility except O-Lab (postgraduates). Uncertain: whether COMP30022 clients are external, current status of MGMT90129, MBS Analytics Lab team format, and 2026 detail for several subjects whose current-year tabs were not indexed.
gaps: Further departmental instances likely exist (other Master of Engineering discipline capstones, e.g. BMEN90018; Master of Climate Science industry project code not found; MDHS/health, education, music/fine arts and social work not searched beyond one handbook query). 2026 eligibility/assessment tabs often not indexed - older-year handbook data used. Partner sector types not documented for most schemes. Relationship between FBE partner-facing 'Industry Projects' (S7) and named subjects (S6, S10) unresolved - possible double count. ARTS90027 2026 status rests on a search summary of the 2026 listing. COMP30022 client externality unverified. MBS (mbs.edu) Analytics Lab treated as University provision.
